title: [Prime] Western Digital WD Red Plus 8TB CMR 3.5 inch Hard Drive $439.25 (RRP $479.26) Delivered @ Amazon JP via AU
body:
Deal: [Prime] Western Digital WD Red Plus 8TB CMR 3.5 inch Hard Drive $439.25 (RRP $479.26) Delivered @ Amazon JP via AU

[adrianhughes1998] Good price in this climate I suppose, hanging out for 4TB ones again though, need 2 of them :(
[buffalo bill] Hang out for the 12tb, it crops up cheaper than this occasionally. Most reds filled with air now which sucks, another 10 or so db louder.
[deangalanoz] This one or the Seagate 10TB Expansion Desktop Hard Drive $360.50
I bought 3 of these and it arrived few days ago. Here is the CrystalDiskInfo
more info: It is a Seagate BarraCuda Pro 10TB, CMR, 7200 RPM and rated at 300 TB/year
Compare to this Western Digital WD Red Plus 8TB, CMR, 5640 RPM but only 180 TB/year
Should i just use the 10tb ones that i already have or buy this dedicated WD Red Plus for NAS?
[YeetFangs] If you are using NAS for backups and file storage or Media library + streaming then use the Seagate BarraCuda Pro 10TB you already have and save yourself some money.
If for other things like running always on apps eg- (docker containers, download clients) then get yourself a dedicated NAS drive for better tuning.
[t25] I never had much luck with Seagate drives. WD/Hitachi on the other hand have always served me well.
[Gwilli] Wonder if the Iron Wolves will come down soon, i mean the shine is going off AI on the stockmarket
[iDroid] Why an Iron Wolf over a WD? They're just too noisy IME.
[TheGodfather-2] Hdd prices going up wasnt in my bingo card.
[cfuse] Every time I ask an LLM a pub quiz question memory, storage, and compute hardware goes up.
[Thermal] Welcome to the present. That's actually a good price.
[s1Lence] I recently bought 4tb and 12tb versions of these for around 160 and 400 respectively so this price doesn't seem very good, better to wait and monitor prices until they drop again, which they frequently do.
[mikuno] Good lord they've been going up lately… mind if you share those deals (even if expired)?
[s1Lence] It was from amazon as well, i just monitor prices (i check many times every day) and if you are active enough you will find good deals but they tend to be low stock so you have to be quick, i use this site to check prices https://diskprices.com/?locale=au
[buffalo bill] Yeah like really quick. Have your payment info pre-saved.
[mikuno] Thanks for the link! Damn the Toshiba 14TB…
[Thermal] @mikuno: Which from the reviews, looks like at least some are undeclared refurbed drives sold as new.
[mikuno] TBH not bad price, I bought some seagate off taobao (brand new, but Thai grey import according to seller/reviews) - incl shipping+GST ended up 180aud for 4TB. I bought two and one arrived DoA, so ended up 35$ out of pocket for return shipping (taobao/sellers typically don't cover international returns), and ordering a replacement would cost another 20-30$ in shipping, making one drive effectively 200$+ for 4TB SeaHawk/IronWolf…
[yewrei] Unfortunately the “Thai grey import” on taobao is usually just refurbished drives that they made look brand new(they are really good at it). Check the serial number seagate’s website.
[Dogstar] I paid $299 2.5 years ago. Do with that information what you will.
They've been a lot less than that too.
https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/844059
I've got a clunky older 4TB that is about to throw a hissy, I reckon. This is gonna be the cheapest they are for a while, right?
[Thermal] The inevitable rationalisation of the AI market to sustainable levels is going to take time to play out, so I can't see these going significantly lower for some time yet. This is a decent discount on what you can by locally, hence I picked up a couple for expanding my NAS.
[Shootinputin89] I paid $300 each for brand new Seagate Exos 10TB drives from Device Deal (aka 5 year warranty/local RMA if required) back in 2022. It's pointless trying to compare to prices past 1.5 years ago because the AI bubble has just ruined everything. This is a 'bargain' only in the current climate. Only buy if you're desperate and have to, otherwise just ignore any of these 'bargains' until we get some actual good prices going again. Though, who knows when that will be..
[OZKap] Do with that information what you will.
Any deals on time machines?
[EspadaV8] Man, I filled my NAS with 8TB drives something like 6-7 years ago thinking by the time it's full I can replace them with much better 16-20TB ones. Now I can't even replace them for the same price. I've taken to doing monthly media pruning to keep some space available. Dreading seeing a status alert pop up.
[t25] Yup I'm in the same boat as you too! Time to get rid of some media I no longer watch
[Gwilli] 11 years ago for me WD Reds 3TB and 4TB now are about the price i paid 11 years ago. Still going strong but i want another NAS for different purposes and the drive costs are huge.
[trevor99] I wouldn't mind guessing the hardware drought has peaked out
https://www.google.com/search?q=western+digital+share+price
[Thermal] True, but their stock price is still 8x what is was in early 2025.
[itsflanno] I got 2x 12tb reds a few weeks ago for 378 from Amazon US.. might have been a price error they sold out almost instantly obviously, but they arrived.
[mrpenpengendo] mine still hasn't shipped. going to wait a bit longer and see what happens.
[Clockwerk] Good thing I didn't pull the trigger for a NAS this year. Guess i'll have to make do with deleting shows and movies for now…
